title: Kernel conductor + KV-shadow weekly synthesis (Sprint 104)
body:
Context:
This note summarizes the Serving Runtime team's weekly synthesis for Sprint 104 focused on the new 'kernel conductor' refactor, KV-shadow experiment runs, and micro-batch heuristics tuning. The aim of the week was to validate that the conductor scheduling reduces tail latency without significantly increasing overall token cost, and to evaluate KV-shadow as a low-risk method to test cache policies against production-like traffic.

Attendees:
- Maya Thompson (owner)
- Lucas Chen (kernel lead)
- Aparna Sinha (batching & telemetry)
- Jonah Patel (SRE / rollout)
- Eleni Ruiz (perf engineer)
- Plus rotating on-call and two backend interns for data collection

High-level summary:
- Kernel conductor refactor landed a minimal-mode scheduler prototype into the branch 'conductor/proto' and ran staged A/B experiments across two dedicated clusters. Initial results show 8–11% lower 95th pct latency for long-context requests (seq_len > 1024) with negligible change to median latency.
- KV-shadow ran three concerted shadow campaigns this week. Shadow traffic mirrored ~7% of production QPS to a shadow cluster configured with a more aggressive slot-eviction policy and a new prefill coalescer. Hit-rate for the shadow cache rose 14% in the 95th percentile sessions, but end-to-end token cost measured in the shadow run increased by 6% due to extra prefill RPCs.
- Micro-batch heuristics tuning (max_batch_age, idle_threshold) produced a mixed bag: reducing max_batch_age from 10ms to 6ms cut p95 by ~4ms for small requests, but under certain arrival patterns it increased small-batch count and raised token cost by ~2%.

Benchmarks & numbers (aggregated):
- Kernel conductor (long-context group): p50=32ms (-1ms), p95=118ms (-11ms), p99=210ms (-22ms). Throughput per-GPU remained within 3% of baseline.
- KV-shadow: session-level cache hit-rate (p95) = 72% (baseline 58%). Token cost per-100k-tokens in shadow config = +6% compared to prod config.
- Batching heuristics: small-req workload p95 latency = 45ms -> 41ms when max_batch_age lowered; however small-batch fraction increased from 12% -> 17%.

Experiment details and notes:
1) Kernel conductor prototype
   - What: Single-threaded conductor that balances kernel invocation order across active partitions to reduce interference from long-sequence sessions.
   - Where: conductor/proto branch, tested on two canary stacks (canary-a, canary-b).
   - Observations: Less tail latency variance; CPU side scheduling cost small (<0.6% CPU). Observed occasional priority inversion when a prefill spike coincided with large KV eviction loops.
   - Follow-ups: Add lightweight priority aging (Lucas). Add telemetry to emit conductor decision traces (Aparna).

2) KV-shadow runs
   - Campaigns: three 24-hour shadows (Tue–Thu) replicating traffic from east-prod over a jittered delay to avoid coupling.
   - Policy tested: aggressive slot-eviction (TTL=60s, slot_count target reduced by 10%), plus coalescer that merges prefill requests for sessions that share prefix hashes.
   - Result: Higher cache hit-rate for long sessions, but increased prefill RPCs on first-touch of coalescer windows; this is the main cause of token-cost uptick.
   - Action: Prototype a debounce window for the coalescer (Eleni) and evaluate a soft-start on eviction to avoid synchronized misses (Jonah).

3) Micro-batch heuristics sweep
   - Sweep params: max_batch_age = {4,6,8,10} ms, idle_threshold = {2,5,10} ms.
   - Finding: For mixed-workload clusters, 6ms max_batch_age gives the best median/tail tradeoff for small requests. For cold-traffic periods, lower idle_threshold is better to reduce spurious small batches.
   - Decision: Default to max_batch_age=6ms for next canary; add dynamic backoff logic when small-batch fraction spikes (Aparna).

Operational incidents:
- 2029-03-18 03:12 UTC: Canary-b experienced a transient p99 spike (~3x) for ~90s during a large-model rollout. Root cause: conductor scheduled a long-context kernel while GC was triggering on a co-located control-plane process. Mitigation: isolate conductor on a dedicated CPU set; SRE to coordinate with release-engineering next rollouts (Jonah).
- No customer-facing degradation observed. Internal alert noise rose due to new conductor trace logs; we tuned sampling to 1/1000 events.

Decisions made this week:
- Proceed to widen kernel conductor canary to 4 clusters after adding priority aging and trace tags (Lucas + Aparna). Target start: 2029-03-25.
- Hold off promoting the aggressive KV eviction policy to prod; instead iterate on coalescer debounce and soft-start eviction.
- Default micro-batch max_batch_age set to 6ms on canaries; dynamic backoff feature to be implemented before wider rollout.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Lucas: Implement priority aging in conductor. ETA 2029-03-24.
- Aparna: Add conductor decision traces, sample at 1/1000 for now. ETA 2029-03-22.
- Eleni: Prototype coalescer debounce (exponential backoff window) and run A/B on shadow. ETA 2029-03-28.
- Jonah: Coordinate CPU pinning for conductor on canary clusters and update runbook. ETA 2029-03-23.
- Maya: Draft rollout plan and post to #serving-runtime for sign-off. ETA 2029-03-21.

Risks & unknowns:
- Conductor interactions with eviction/GC cycles are not fully modeled; risk of rare priority inversions remains. Need longer-running soak tests.
- Shadow runs show cost regressions in edge-cases; we need to measure end-to-end application-level utility (quality regressions if any) before pushing cache policy changes to prod.

Notes / reminders:
- Perf data and raw traces stored in perf-bucket/2029-03-conductor-shadow (link in linked_artifacts).
- Please review PR 3381 focusing on the conductor scheduling algorithm (code comments requested).
- Next sync: Wednesday 2029-03-27 10:00 PT — bring updated traces and the first coalescer debounce prototype results.

Appendix (short):
- Quick checklist for canary expansion: CPU pinning applied (Y/N) — Jonah to confirm; conductor trace sampling confirmed (Aparna); dynamic batch backoff merged to branch (TBD).


This doc is a working synthesis; notes to self and open threads are intentionally loose. If anything needs to be promoted into the runbook or the postmortem, flag it in the weekly triage channel.
